newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors probe Hansol Group - paper.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors probe Hansol Group - paper.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors are probing the Hansol Group in connection with a scandal swirling around President Kim Young-sam's second son, the Chosun Ilbo newspaper reported on Wednesday.

It said prosecutors had been told by officials of the country's 16th largest industrial conglomerate the group managed a seven billion won fund on behalf of a former top intelligence official linked to the son, Kim Hyun-chul. A group public relations official would neither confirm nor deny the report.
The Hansol official said senior group executives were meeting on Wednesday to discuss the report.
"At the moment, I don't know whether it's true or not. I expect an official explanation from group management later," said the public relations official, who declined to be identified.
The Chosun Ilbo, citing unnamed prosecution officials, said several Hansol officials had been questioned by prosecutors and admitted to having managed the fund since 1993.
It named the intelligence official as Kim Ki-sup, who stepped down this year amid allegations that he fed confidential reports to the president's son. Kim Ki-sup denied the allegations.
